newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP okays Bruce oilfield expansion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP okays Bruce oilfield expansion.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said its board had conditionally approved a project to assess the phase two development of the western area of the Bruce oil and gas field in the North Sea.

The development, which would allow for the access of oil and gas reserves on the Western Area of the field is subject to the approval of the other partners in the project and the British government's Department of Trade and Industry, BHP said.
The British Petroleum Co Plc holds a majority 37 percent stake in the Bruce field and is the operator.
ELF Aquitaine holds 31.5 percent, BHP's BHP Petroleum Ltd 16 percent, Total Oil Marine 11.75 percent and Veba AG unit Deminex 3.75 percent.

Planned capital expenditure of A$132 million net to BHP would be to expand the existing Bruce Field facilities to develop 116 billion standard cubic feet of gas and 10 million barrels of condensate, also net to BHP, with production starting in 1998, the company said.

Production from the first phase of the Bruce field commenced in 1993, with gas supplied under contractual commitments to British Gas Plc and Corby Power Ltd and liquids sold under long term contract to British Petroleum.
For the six months to 30 November 1996, average daily production net to BHP Petroleum was 88 million standard cubic feet of gas and 5,500 barrels of liquids.

"Development of the Western Area will enable the joint venture to extend the deliverability of gas to its customers at the maximum contract rate (688 million standard cubic feet per day) from 1998 to 2004," BHP said.
Liquids production is expected to increase to 8,200 barrels of liquids per day at peak output, the company said.
The Bruce field extends across three exploration licence blocks in the United Kingdom: 9/8a, 9/9a and 9/9b, located 350 km north east of Aberdeen.
